def test_make_key_changes_on_any_input():
    k1 = make_key("text", "p", "c")
    k2 = make_key("text", "p", "c")
    assert k1 == k2, "Same inputs should produce same key"

def test_make_key_different_text_changes_key():
    k1 = make_key("text1", "p", "c")
    k2 = make_key("text2", "p", "c")
    assert k1 != k2, "Different text should produce different key"

def test_make_key_different_profile_changes_key():
    k1 = make_key("text", "p1", "c")
    k2 = make_key("text", "p2", "c")
    assert k1 != k2, "Different profile should produce different key"

def test_make_key_different_criteria_changes_key():
    k1 = make_key("text", "p", "c1")
    k2 = make_key("text", "p", "c2")
    assert k1 != k2, "Different criteria should produce different key"

def test_make_key_handles_none_inputs():
    k1 = make_key(None, None, None)
    k2 = make_key("", "", "")
    # Both None inputs and empty strings should be handled
    assert len(k1) == 16, "Key should be 16 characters"
    assert isinstance(k1, str), "Key should be string"

def test_make_key_consistent_with_none_and_empty():
    k1 = make_key(None, None, None)
    k2 = make_key("", "", "")
    # Both should produce consistent results (deterministic)
    assert len(k1) == 16
    assert len(k2) == 16
    assert k1 == k1  # Self-consistency check

def test_make_key_no_ambiguous_keys():
    # Ensure different combinations don't collide
    keys = []
    for t in ["a", "b"]:
        for p in ["x", "y"]:
            for c in ["1", "2"]:
                k = make_key(t, p, c)
                keys.append(k)
    # All should be unique
    assert len(keys) == len(set(keys)), "All key combinations should produce unique keys"

    from service import score
    store = {}
    compute_called = []
    
    def compute1():
        compute_called.append(1)
        return 100
    
    def compute2():
        compute_called.append(2)
        return 200
    
    # First call - should compute
    result1 = score(store, "text", "p", "c", compute1)
    assert result1 == 100
    assert len(compute_called) == 1
    
    # Second call with same inputs - should reuse cache
    result2 = score(store, "text", "p", "c", compute2)
    assert result2 == 100
    assert len(compute_called) == 1  # Still only 1 computation
    
    # Third call with different text - should recompute
    result3 = score(store, "text2", "p", "c", compute2)
    assert result3 == 200
    assert len(compute_called) == 2  # Now 2 computations

    store = {}

        return 100
    
    # First call with None inputs
